measured.condition: GitHub Actions, run 32300811749, job 'suite-and-guards (ubuntu-22.04)' on main after P5.1 and P8.3 merged; workflow unchanged (pinned threads, dev extra only, CityFlow not built, no corpus, no SUMO binary)
measured.result: 1100 passed, 98 skipped, read from the job's own summary line. Both matrix legs (ubuntu-22.04 and ubuntu-24.04) failed on this gate; libc-matrix passed.
measured.breakdown: DERIVED, not recounted, and it RECONCILES: 32 cityflow + 54 corpus/checkpoint + 10 SUMO + 2 matplotlib = 98. Only the corpus term moved (28 -> 54, +26) because P5.1 added corpus-gated tests and no cityflow-, SUMO- or matplotlib-gated ones. Cross-checked independently: a corpus-absent run on the P5.2 worktree attributes exactly 26 skips to P5.1's two files (test_joint_windows 14 + test_spatial_mixing 12), which equals the observed delta.
measured.why_not_recounted_from_the_log: The runner's -rs block aggregates parametrised skips as 'SKIPPED [N] file:line: reason' and gh run view --log duplicates lines, so a category sum taken from the log does not reproduce the summary total. A wrong breakdown in this file is worse than none, so the derivation above is used instead and is stated as derived.

superseded.why_it_was_wrong: Not wrong -- EXPIRED EXACTLY AS PREDICTED. The 2026-08-17 entry declared 're_measure_required_at: merge of P5.1' and forecast 'roughly +25 skips ... this ceiling WILL breach on that merge, and it is meant to'. Observed delta: +26. The mechanism worked; the number was stale.

its_own_superseded.why_it_was_wrong: It came from a simulated runner on the dev machine, and the simulation was defeated by usrmerge: the harness removed `sumo` from a symlink copy of /usr/bin but left /bin on PATH, and /bin IS /usr/bin on this system, so shutil.which('sumo') kept finding it and 10 SUMO-gated tests ran that a runner skips. The error was invisible locally and was caught by the first real run -- which is the reason the ceiling was declared provisional and the branch was pushed.

ceiling_is_a_consequence_of: the workflow does NOT build the vendored CityFlow (coordinator ruling 2026-08-17: an unverified C++ build step is a new failure surface on the one task whose purpose is reliability). 32 of these 72 skips are cityflow-gated, so building it would move the ceiling from 72 to 40.

no corpus is available on a runner: datasets*/ is gitignored and ~189 MB, so 28 corpus- and checkpoint-gated tests skip. That 28 independently reproduces the coordinator's 2026-08-16 corpus-absent measurement.

SUMO is not installed on the runner, so _sumo_available() is False and 10 SUMO-backed tests skip cleanly. sumolib IS present -- traci declares sumolib>=1.27.1 and pip resolved it -- so the gate here is the missing binary, not the missing module.
the workflow installs the dev extra only, so the 2 matplotlib-gated tests skip.

re_measure_required_at.reason: tests/test_tier_sweep.py is 89 tests and contains exactly ONE skip site: a single test function with an inline pytest.skip('the secured output/p5_1 tree is not present on this machine'). It has ZERO cityflow references and, checked on the branch under the corpus-absent condition, contributes ZERO corpus-gated skips -- P5.2's tests are synthetic. So the expected observation at that merge is 99, not a large jump.
re_measure_required_at.what_to_do: Re-measure and commit 99 deliberately. DO NOT pre-bump the ceiling to absorb the +1: a one-skip breach is exactly the size that invites slack, and slack is what blinds the gate.
re_measure_required_at.mandated_by: coordinator ruling on BRIEF_23 Q1, 2026-08-17 -- 'a ceiling whose expiry lives only in a chat is a ceiling that silently breaches'. Restated 2026-08-19 after the P5.1 expiry fired correctly.

pytest.how_to_update: Read the observed count from the failing job's summary, re-measure deliberately, and commit the new value together with the reason in the same commit. Never widen it with slack: slack is what blinds the gate.

english.why_not_zero: P0.9, still open: the o-acute false positive. THREE of these four are the guard's own documentation of the character class it detects, quoted in claude_guard.sh and in two committed patches; de-diacriticising them would corrupt a record. The fourth is .claude/agents/master-coordinator.md, which carries a Polish WORD ('skonczone', with n-acute) inside an illustrative quotation, not a name -- checked, not assumed.
english.pending_patch: 4 is the POST-APPLY total and requires docs/patches/check_english_mikolaj.patch, which adds 'Mikolaj' to ALLOWED_NAMES. Until a human applies it the tree measures 6 and THIS GATE REPORTS A MISMATCH ON PURPOSE, so the pending action cannot be forgotten. The regression that took it from the recorded 5 to 6 is docs/returns/P8.3.md:141, where the packet documents the allowlist gap BY WRITING THE NAME, making the sentence an instance of the defect it describes. Applying clears two hits (README.md:30 and that line), both carrying l-stroke and n-acute from 'Mikolaj Wolinski'.

frozen_guard.why: The guard derives everything from `git status --porcelain`, which is clean on a fresh checkout, so on a runner it always passes and proves nothing. It is invoked anyway because its absence would be worse, and the workflow says so at the call site rather than letting a green tick imply more than it proves. A PR-diff variant is a NEW enforcement mechanism and needs its own authorisation -- coordinator ruling 2026-08-17, parked as a DEFERRED row.
